text: Initial hypothesis from abstract scan: Apply Q mechanism design (unknown capabilities, peer scoring, reward shaping) to harden P credit assignment against strategic manipulation like sandbagging. Q explicitly lists sandbagging + reward shaping as applications; P uses potential-based reward shaping with LMM-generated comparisons. Key question: Is P vulnerable to strategic manipulation that Q mechanisms could address? Tension: P assumes cooperative MARL, Q handles misaligned incentives.

Q provides mechanism design tools for unknown capabilities/alignment with specific applications to sandbagging, peer scoring, and reward shaping. Key insight: one-sided imitation structure (capabilities can be concealed but not counterfeited) enables revelation principle and conditions for disciplining multiple agents via higher-order beliefs. P provides MARL credit assignment via rank aggregation using LMM-generated comparisons, converted to potential-based reward shaping. Critical tension: P assumes cooperative MARL with honest LMM-generated comparisons; Q addresses strategic agents who may conceal capabilities. The abstract scan hypothesis has merit but needs sharpening: Q mechanisms could harden P against strategic manipulation IF agents in P setting have incentives to manipulate comparisons.
